anomalies.observed: On both M5Stack bus connectors the '+5V' net arrow is attached to pin 25, while pin 27 carries only the default unconnected name 'PIN27' (no net). The BAT net is correctly on pin 29 and TXD2/RXD2 on 15/16, so the pin-numbering convention matches the specification everywhere except the 5V pin.
anomalies.expected: The specification states the board's +5V rail 'is also tied directly to J1/J2 pin 27 (the M5Stack bus's 5V pin)', so +5V should connect to pin 27, not pin 25, and pin 27 should not be left floating.

evidence.quote: The same +5V net is also tied directly to J1/J2 pin 27 (the M5Stack bus's 5V pin), so +5V is effectively the logical OR of 'M5Stack-supplied 5V' and 'external 5V input via D1'.
J1/J2 Conn_02x15_Odd_Even: '+5V' arrow on the PIN25 row, 'PIN27' row has no net, 'BAT' arrow on the PIN29 row (sheet m5-pantilt, page 1).

anomalies.impact: When powered from an M5Stack Core, the Core's 5V bus pin (27) is not connected to the board's +5V rail, so the +5V rail and the diode-isolated servo rail (D2 / C1-C4 / J3,J8 pin2) receive no power from the Core and the servos cannot run unless an external 5V supply is plugged into J7. At the same time the board's +5V rail is instead driven onto bus pin 25, which is not the M5Stack 5V pin, so it back-feeds/conflicts with whatever signal pin 25 carries and the documented 5V pass-through to stacked modules is broken.

parsed.summary: All component values, the PWM/serial jumper scheme, the MAX3485 auto-direction circuit, and the power paths match the specification, but the +5V rail is wired to M5Stack bus pin 25 instead of the specified pin 27 (leaving pin 27 unconnected), which breaks the Core-powered 5V/servo-rail supply and the 5V pass-through.
